title: A Crocodile Bites With 3,700 Pounds of Force (Hardest Ever Measured)

scenes.text: A crocodile bites with 3,700 pounds of force.
That's the hardest bite ever measured on a living animal. Like a small car's weight clamping down.
Scientists wrestled 83 crocs and alligators onto a bite meter to find out. The saltwater croc won.
Its jaw muscles are built almost entirely for closing. Once it clamps, it doesn't let go.
And its ancestors were worse. A 40 foot extinct croc bit with 23,000 pounds. 3,700 is the small one.

description:
A saltwater crocodile bites with 3,700 pounds of force, the strongest bite ever measured on a living animal.
Researchers at Florida State University restrained 83 adult crocodiles and alligators and placed a bite-force meter between their back teeth. A 17-foot saltwater crocodile set the record; a 13-foot American alligator managed 2,980 pounds. The team estimates extinct 35 to 40 foot crocodilians bit with about 23,000 pounds.
Which animal do you think bites harder: a crocodile or a hippo? Comment below.
first_comment: The same study found the crocodile's teeth press down at about 350,000 psi. Would you rather face a crocodile on land or in the water?
